drafted_from: tool:keep-a-mail-attachment's own row in tools/read-and-write-mail/tool-rows.json, read-data/mail.mjs (keepAMailAttachment) and the Gmail and AgentMail adapters; the answer is the shape those operations produce for the sample input
start_here: Say to your AI: "Keep the PDF that was sent to my mail inbox as a file." It finds the message with find-mail, then runs tool:keep-a-mail-attachment as that account and gets back the name, size, media type and BLAKE3 identity of the kept file.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it asks the mail provider for one attachment of one message and keeps its bytes as a file of the run.
instructions: 1. Find the message: say "Find the mail with the PDF in it" and let your AI call tool:find-mail with its provider and the words of its subject.
2. Read the message with tool:read-a-mail and note its attachment's id from the attachments list (its name, type and size are there).
3. Say "Keep that attachment" and let your AI call tool:keep-a-mail-attachment with the provider, your account handle, the message id and the attachment id.
4. To choose the kept output's display name, give name (for example guide.pdf). The Files keeper uses it as one plain name inside this tool's output folder; it is not an absolute destination path.

5. Read files.attachment.name for the actual Files name and files.attachment.identity for its content identity. result.name is the attachment's display name, not proof of placement. The file is kept as data; nothing in it is opened or run.
6. For a file already kept, use tool:your-files move_names with its source version, check the target independently, and then update any resource row. Do not download the attachment again to move it.
7. A provider that does not offer the job (Outlook) says so in words and nothing is fetched.

worked_examples.title: Keep the PDF attached to a mail
worked_examples.ask: Keep the PDF attached to that mail as a file.
worked_examples.given: A mail in the inbox with one PDF attachment named guide.pdf of 5 bytes, the provider answering from a recorded reply.
worked_examples.hands_back: It kept the file and answered {"name":"guide.pdf","bytes":5,"media_type":"application/pdf","blake3":"<64 hex characters>"}.
